# Design Review: Minimalist Blog Website

## Review scope

Reviewed [requirements.md](./requirements.md) against [architecture.md](./architecture.md), including functional coverage, security boundaries, and unresolved decisions.

## Overall assessment

**Proceed with follow-ups.** The modular-monolith design is appropriate for the stated scope and includes the critical trusted-server boundaries for authentication, ownership checks, and post input handling. No blocking architectural defect was identified. Resolve the medium-priority behavior details below during implementation planning so tests and the UI implement one consistent interpretation.

## Coverage assessment

| Requirement area | Assessment | Evidence / notes |
|---|---|---|
| Registration and login | Covered | Registration/login endpoints, uniqueness constraints, password hashing, and expected success/error responses are defined. |
| Persistent sessions, timeout, logout | Covered | Server-side sessions, cookie protections, activity tracking, 30-minute expiry, rotation, and invalidation are described. |
| Browse and read | Covered | Public feed and post detail endpoints; summary fields and full reading view are included. |
| Search and sort | Covered | Server-side title/content search and allowlisted title/date sort modes are specified. |
| Create, edit, delete | Covered | API, timestamp behavior, confirmation requirement context, and server-side author ownership are addressed; see UI follow-up. |
| Security | Covered | The design calls for secure password storage, protected cookies, CSRF protection, parameterized queries, safe rendering, and server-side authorization. |
| Out-of-scope features | Covered by omission | Image upload, OTP reset, and WYSIWYG editing are not added. |

## Findings and recommendations

### Medium — Specify feed chronology and date shown on each post

The requirements call for a chronological feed, display a published/modified date, and separately allow sorting by modified date. The architecture says “chronological” but does not explicitly name the default ordering column or which timestamp the card displays after an edit. These interpretations can produce different feed order and card labels.

**Recommendation:** Use `createdAt DESC` for the default chronological feed; show the published/created date for unedited posts and the modified date for edited posts, with a clear “Updated” indicator. Keep the explicit modified-date sort modes based on `modifiedAt`. Confirm this product interpretation before implementation or document the chosen convention in the implementation plan.

### Medium — Make required navigation and delete confirmation explicit in UI flows

The API contract defines operations, but the user-visible success flow is not fully mapped. In particular, registration must return the user to Login, successful login must go to Home, logout must return to Login, and deletion must prompt for confirmation before the request is sent.

**Recommendation:** Include these route transitions and the delete-confirm/cancel behavior in the UI implementation tasks and acceptance tests. A cancel action must make no delete request.

### Low — Define and consistently enforce the password minimum

The minimum length is intentionally left open in the architecture. Requirements explicitly require client-side minimum-length validation, while the server is the trusted validation boundary.

**Recommendation:** Select a concrete minimum during planning and apply the same rule in both client and server validation. Treat server validation as authoritative.

### Low — Bound feed and search inputs

The design correctly calls for server validation and explicit input limits but does not set values. An unbounded post content or search query can cause avoidable storage or query load.

**Recommendation:** Set reasonable maximum lengths for title, content, and search query during implementation planning, validate them on the server, and cover boundary cases in tests. Pagination may remain deferred unless expected data volume requires it.

## Security review notes

- Author identity is derived from the authenticated session, not request fields.
- UI-only edit/delete controls are correctly treated as non-authoritative.
- Session expiry and logout invalidate server-side session state.
- Cookie-authenticated state-changing requests are required to have CSRF defenses.
- Safe output handling and parameterized search are explicitly addressed.
- Password hashing, session cookie configuration, and request limits must be verified in implementation; this document review does not validate runtime behavior.

## Suggested implementation exit criteria

- Tests cover owner and non-owner create/edit/delete behavior at the server/API boundary.
- Tests cover session refresh persistence, logout invalidation, and 30-minute inactivity expiry.
- Tests verify all sort modes, title/content search, and no-results behavior.
- UI tests verify registration/login/logout navigation and delete confirmation/cancellation.
- Client and server enforce the same selected password policy and input limits.
- The default feed ordering and timestamp label follow the selected convention above.
